newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Yeltsin, Chernomyrdin discuss army reform.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Yeltsin, Chernomyrdin discuss army reform.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin discussed army reforms, Afghanistan and an electricity workers' strike in Russia's Far East on Tuesday, the presidential press service said.
The two men also discussed the government's budget plans during talks at the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow where the 65-year-old president is preparing for a heart bypass operation.

The press service said in a statement that Yeltsin had expressed satisfaction with the work of the new Defence Council, which discussed reforms and funding of the armed forces at its first session last Friday.
The president expressed concern at the situation in the cash-strapped armed forces last week and security chief Alexander Lebed has said there is a danger of a mutiny in the army.

Chernomyrdin also briefed Yeltsin on talks last Friday on Afghanistan among representatives of the 12-member Commonwealth of Independent States in the Kazakh capital, Almaty. The Afghan capital Kabul has been captured by the Islamic fundamentalist movement Taleban.
He updated Yeltsin on measures being taken by the government to ease electricity problems in the far eastern Primorsky region where power workers say they have temporarily ended a strike.

Yeltsin moved to Barvikha at the weekend after three weeks in Moscow's Central Clinical Hospital. He announced on September 5 that he would have a heart operation and his doctors expect the surgery to go ahead in the next five to nine weeks.
The operation will involve grafting in new veins to bypass blocked coronary arteries and improve the supply of blood to Yeltsin's heart.
